subject: European History
title: 11. Post-War Settlements, United Nations, Marshall Plan, Germany, NATO and Decolonization

segments.text: The decade after 1945 was simultaneously reconstruction and Cold War division — these two processes happened together, not sequentially, and the topic’s institutions (UN, Marshall Plan, NATO, divided Germany) should be studied as interconnected elements of one emerging order.

items.text: The 1947–48 U.S. aid programme supporting Western European recovery, rejected by the Soviet Union for its own bloc.
The founding institution of postwar European economic integration.
Create a 1945–55 timeline explaining how reconstruction and Cold War division happened simultaneously; map occupation zones and divided Germany.
Practise one analytical outline answering: “How were the Marshall Plan, divided Germany, and NATO interconnected elements of the same emerging Cold War order?”
Do not study the Marshall Plan, Germany and NATO as unrelated events; they were interconnected elements of the emerging Cold War order.
Do not say decolonisation happened only because Europe was weak; nationalist movements and changing international norms were also decisive.
Do not confuse the UN with NATO; the former is a global organisation, the latter a military alliance.
The United Nations was established in 1945.
The Marshall Plan was announced in 1947; aid began in 1948.
The Federal Republic of Germany and German Democratic Republic were created in 1949.
NATO was founded in 1949; the European Coal and Steel Community was created in 1951.
Treat reconstruction and Cold War division as simultaneous, interconnected processes, not sequential stages.
The European Coal and Steel Community (1951) is the essential institutional seed for the entire European integration story continued in Topics 12 and 13.
